ostracize

OS-truh-size · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To ostracize is to deliberately exclude someone from a group.

After the scandal broke, former colleagues began to ostracize him at every industry event.

Example

The new student was ostracized by her classmates for weeks simply because she'd moved from a different state.

Ostracize describes a group's collective decision, whether openly agreed on or just an unspoken habit, to shut one person out.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

shun: To shun someone is to deliberately avoid them, and a single person can do it alone, quietly and without ceremony. To ostracize takes a group: classmates, colleagues, or a whole town collectively shutting one person out. One avoider shuns; it takes a community to ostracize.

exclude: To exclude is simply to keep someone out of something -- a game, a meeting, a club -- and it can happen once, even politely. To ostracize is a sustained social punishment: the group deliberately cuts a person out of its company and keeps them out.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

embrace: welcome someone warmly

include: make someone part of a group

Where it sits · how formal and lasting the exclusion

ignore → ostracize → banish

ignore vs. ostracize: Ignore sits at the mild end of exclusion: ignoring someone can be a single moment of inattention, far milder than ostracizing them, which is a group's lasting, deliberate act of shutting one person out.

banish vs. ostracize: To banish someone is to formally and permanently expel them, a more official step than simply ostracizing them socially.

Which word fits?

Answer correctly to continue.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — ostrac: a broken piece of pottery used as a ballot (Greek (ostrakon))

suffix — -ize: to make, to cause to become (Greek)

Put it together: ostrac ("pottery ballot," from Greek ostrakon) + -ize ("to make") = to vote someone out, as ancient Athenians once did.

Why there's no relative to spot: Ostracize is built on ostrakon, the Greek name for a shard of broken clay from a jar or cup. Athenians wrote names on these shards the way we might use slips of paper. Ostrakon never became an everyday English word — which is why ostracize has no common relative to spot.

Word Building

Word Choice

Ostracize describes exclusion driven by a group, whether a school, a workplace, or a whole community -- compare this to "excommunicate," which is specifically a formal religious expulsion, and "estrange," which is about one person drifting apart from someone close to them.
